title: Knowledge Check 1 - Lessons 1-5
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 1-5 - Prompt Engineering. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A requirement asks for a currency-converted amount that must be exact and recalculates every time an Opportunity is saved. Which surface fits it?
options: A formula field that recomputes the value on every save
A prompt template in Prompt Builder grounded in the Opportunity record
An agent action that asks a model for the converted amount
A Data 360 calculated insight refreshed on a nightly schedule
questions.explanation: Compute the truth, then phrase it: an exact value that a rule can compute belongs in a formula, a Flow or a report, while a prompt template is the tool when the deliverable is generated language grounded in record data. Asking a model to do arithmetic makes the build slower, less predictable and harder to defend in review.

questions.question: A requirement asks for a personalized welcome email drafted from each Contact record, tailored in tone and reused across the sales team. Which tool fits?
options: A formula field on Contact
A validation rule
A scheduled Flow that updates a field
A prompt template in Prompt Builder, grounded in the Contact record
questions.explanation: The requirement is generated language grounded in record data, which is exactly the shape Prompt Builder serves, while a formula, a validation rule, and a Flow compute or enforce values rather than generate prose.

questions.question: The exam guide recommends which certification as a foundation for this exam, while stating it is not required?
options: Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator
Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist itself
Salesforce Certified Marketing Cloud Administrator
Salesforce Certified Data 360 Consultant
questions.explanation: The guide lists the Salesforce Certified Platform Administrator (and Platform App Builder) as recommended, not required, while the general platform primer stays out of scope for this course.

questions.question: A business wants the days-to-renewal value on every account to be an exact number that never varies, and separately wants a plain-language note explaining the renewal risk. Which approach fits?
options: One prompt template that outputs both the number and the note
A formula field for both values
A Flow or formula computes days-to-renewal, and a prompt template grounded in that value writes the risk note
A report that lists the renewal notes
questions.explanation: The exact number belongs to a deterministic computation while the explanation is generated language, so the correct pattern is compute first and phrase second rather than asking a model for the number.

questions.question: A requirement says that whenever an opportunity reaches Closed Won, the system must set a related record and notify the owner in a fixed order. Which tool is correct?
options: A deterministic Flow, because the requirement changes records and enforces a sequence
A prompt template in Prompt Builder
A report filtered on Closed Won
A Field Generation template
questions.explanation: A prompt template returns text and does not act on records, so a requirement that updates records in a defined order belongs to Flow.

questions.question: Which requirement shape points at Prompt Builder rather than a report, a formula, or a Flow?
options: Show the total pipeline value by stage
Compute a discount from list price
Update a field when a case closes
Draft a personalized follow-up email and summarize call notes, adapted to each record
questions.explanation: Free-text output that must adapt to each record and needs drafting or summarization is the shape Prompt Builder serves, while totals, discounts, and record updates belong to reports, formulas, and Flow.

questions.question: An admin needs to let a group of service reps run an already-built prompt template without letting them edit it. Which permission set fits?
options: Prompt Template Manager
Prompt Template User
Customize Application
Modify All Data
questions.explanation: The Prompt Template User permission set grants only Execute Prompt Templates, which is run-without-author, while Prompt Template Manager adds authoring and Customize Application is unnecessarily broad.

questions.question: A user holds Execute Prompt Templates, but when they try to run a template nothing is available. What is the most likely cause?
options: They also need Manage Prompt Templates
They need the Customize Application permission
No version of the template is active
They need Modify All Data
questions.explanation: A prompt template is unavailable to users until a version is activated, so run permission alone does not publish it, and authoring permission is irrelevant to the gate.

questions.question: At run time, which data can a prompt template ground into its prompt?
options: Any record in the org, because prompts run in system context
Only records the template author can see
Only records from Data 360, never standard objects
The records and fields the executing user is permitted to see, per sharing and field-level security
questions.explanation: Access to merge data is governed by the permissions of the executing user, so sharing rules and field-level security still apply and a prompt is not a route around them.

questions.question: A rep can open a Case but cannot read the Internal Notes field. They run an activated Case Summary template whose prompt centers on Internal Notes. What happens, and why?
options: The template fails for everyone, because a field is missing
The rep sees the notes anyway, because prompts run as the author
The rep sees the notes because the template is activated
The rep gets a summary missing that field, because field-level security filters the executing user's grounding
questions.explanation: Access to merge data is governed by the executing user's permissions, so field-level security removes the field for that runner while leaving the template unchanged for others.

questions.question: A manager authors and activates a template, runs Preview, and it looks perfect. End users later get a shorter summary. What is the cause?
options: The template was never activated
Preview ran with the author's access, and the end users have less record or field access
The end users lack Execute Prompt Templates
The manager granted Customize Application by mistake
questions.explanation: Preview executes with the author's own access, so it does not reveal the access gap a lower-privilege runner will hit, which is why you test as a representative runner.

questions.question: An admin is asked to let reps run a published template and nothing else. What is the correct grant?
options: Assign the Prompt Template User permission set, which grants only Execute Prompt Templates
Assign Customize Application
Assign the Prompt Template Manager permission set
Assign Modify All Data
questions.explanation: Prompt Template User grants only the run permission, while Manager adds authoring and the other two options grant far more than running a template requires.

questions.question: A requirement is to fill a Next Step text field on an Opportunity record page with a generated suggestion when a user clicks a button. Which template type fits?
options: Field Generation, which binds one object and writes generated text into a record field
Sales Email, which drafts an email
Record Summary, which summarizes a record
Flex, which defines its own multi-object resources
questions.explanation: The output lands in a field on a single record and is triggered from the record page, which is exactly what Field Generation is built for.

questions.question: A requirement must combine an Account, its Opportunities, and a custom Product object into one generated recommendation, and the output is used outside a record field. Which type fits?
options: Field Generation
Record Summary
Flex, which can define multiple objects as resources and is invoked from Flow, Apex, or a prompt action
Sales Email
questions.explanation: Flex is the type that defines its own resources and can ground with more than one object, while Field Generation and Record Summary bind a single object and Sales Email binds a Contact or Lead.

questions.question: Which statement about a prompt template type is correct?
options: You can switch a template between types after creating it
The type is chosen at creation and fixes which objects you can bind and where the template can be invoked
Every type binds to exactly one object
The type has no effect on entry points
questions.explanation: The type is selected once, at creation, and it determines the binding and the entry points, with Flex allowing multiple objects, so it cannot be changed later and it does affect entry points.
